prompt: A Karplus–Strong patch sounds too low. You shorten its delay line while keeping the sample rate and damping settings fixed. What should you expect?

options.text: A lower pitch, because fewer samples contain less energy
options.explanation: Stored energy affects decay and level; the shorter loop repeats sooner.

options.text: A higher pitch, with precise tuning still depending on the loop filter’s delay
options.explanation: Correct. Shortening the loop raises the repetition rate. The filter contributes delay too.

options.text: Only a louder note, with no pitch change
options.explanation: The delay is part of the pitch-setting feedback loop, not just a volume control.

options.text: Exact tuning from the integer delay length alone
options.explanation: Whole-sample delay choices and filter delay limit exact tuning; fractional delay may be needed.

workedExample: Follow one trip around the loop. A shorter trip lets the pattern repeat more often, so pitch rises. Include the filter’s delay when tuning; the delay-line length alone is only an approximation.
